q: Does adding slag to cement raw meal cut calcination CO2?
title: Slag in raw meal: calcination CO2
short: Yes. Calcination CO2 comes only from carbonates such as limestone. Calcium supplied by already decarbonated material, like steel slag or fly ash in the raw meal, releases no CO2 in the kiln, so CO2 per tonne of clinker falls.
audience: Cement plants in Turkey, India and elsewhere using steel slag or other decarbonated materials in kiln feed

p: The IPCC default links clinker CO2 to its lime content on the assumption that all the lime came from carbonate. If part of the lime comes from slag, that share released no CO2, so the default overstates emissions.

ul: Use a raw meal based method: carbonate content of the kiln feed, measured by lab analysis.
Or adjust the clinker based factor for non carbonate calcium, with slag tonnes and its CaO content.

p: The lower calcination figure counts only with measurements a verifier can check. Keep raw meal and slag analyses for the year.
